blocks.text: For centuries, sundials and water clocks inaccurately told us all we needed to know about time. Mechanical clocks started appearing on towers in Italy in the 14th century, but their timekeeping was less impressive than their looks, wandering up to 15 minutes a day. By the 17th century some geniuses, including Galileo and Pascal, had theorized about, but failed to build, better timepieces. Then, in 1656, Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens constructed the first pendulum clock, revolutionizing timekeeping. The precision of Huygens’ clock allowed scientists to use it for their physics experiments, and shopkeepers to open and close at fixed hours. In 1761, Englishman John Harrison perfected a clock that worked at sea and put accurate time in a navigator’s pocket.

readingSentences.english: Then, in 1656, Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens constructed the first pendulum clock, revolutionizing timekeeping.
readingSentences.korean: 그러다가 1656년에 네덜란드의 천문학자 Christiaan Huygens가 최초의 추시계를 만들어 시간을 맞추는 것에 대변혁을 일으켰다.

readingSentences.english: The precision of Huygens’ clock allowed scientists to use it for their physics experiments, and shopkeepers to open and close at fixed hours.
readingSentences.korean: Huygens의 시계의 정확성은 과학자들이 그들의 물리학 실험을 위해 그것을 사용하게 했고 가게 주인들이 정해진 시간에 문을 열고 닫게 해주었다.

readingSentences.english: In 1761, Englishman John Harrison perfected a clock that worked at sea and put accurate time in a navigator’s pocket.
readingSentences.korean: 1761년에 영국인 John Harrison은 바다에서 작동하는 시계를 완성해서 정확한 시간을 항해자의 호주머니 속에 넣어주었다.
